title: Heterogeneous Target Metric Synthesis and Safety Budgets for Dedicated Autoscaler
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Our Dedicated product needs autoscaling policies that can simultaneously satisfy per-tenant throughput guarantees and minimize cost. Current single-metric scaling (e.g., CPU or p95 latency alone) leads to oscillation during bursty traffic and either wasted capacity or missed SLOs.

Goal: Design and implement an autoscaling policy engine that synthesizes multiple target metrics (percentiles, throughput, concurrency, queue depth), derives a unified scale recommendation, and enforces safety budgets (surge credits, hard caps, cooldown windows). The engine must be explainable, simulatable offline, and support per-tenant overrides.

Scope: Prototype policy compiler + runtime evaluator + simulation harness + runtime flags for gradual rollout. This ticket covers policy design, metric selection heuristics, safety budget model, and implementation spike for a runtime plugin. Full rollout and UI will be follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine produces deterministic scale decisions in tests given synthetic metric traces
95th percentile tail latency (p95) SLO >= 99% for workloads with configured throughput guarantees under recorded replay tests
Autoscaler overshoot (extra vCPU/GPU capacity beyond needed) <= 25% on synthetic step-burst workloads compared to baseline greedy scaler
Safety budgets prevent more than 2 sustained surge expansions within a 10-minute window per tenant unless tenant has elevated surge allocation
Integration tests validate policy with real telemetry names: p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_second, queued_requests, effective_throughput, gpu_util_pct
Documentation describing policy rules, configuration schema, and rollback steps is checked into the repo
tasks: Draft policy spec: metric aggregation, prioritization, and tie-breaking rules
Design safety budget primitives: surge_credits, hard_cap, min_idle_capacity, cooldown_window
Implement policy compiler that converts high-level policy to runtime evaluation graph
Add simulator harness to replay historical tenant traces and measure decision quality
Instrument runtime to report decision explanations (why scaled, primary metric, projected headroom)
Create integration test suite with synthetic workload generator
Run perf replay on three representative tenants (PLG-app, mid-market SaaS, enterprise batch) and capture dashboards
comments: 2025-02-13 - Initial spec drafted. Focus on combining percentile and throughput targets rather than raw utilization. Ava: propose surge_credits model to smooth spikes.
2025-02-18 - Architecture review: decided to keep policy compiler declarative and deterministic. Marcus: prefer quantile smoothing over exponential moving averages to preserve tail behavior.
2025-02-24 - Spike simulation results: naive p95-only policy caused 3x overshoot under synthetic long-tail burst. New composite scoring reduced overshoot by ~40%.
2025-02-27 - PR opened for simulator and compiler stubs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1428
2025-03-01 - Ops request: add emergency-evict flag to bypass surge credits for noisy noisy-tenant scenarios. Flag gated behind rollout.
2025-03-02 - Implemented decision explanation logging prototype; needs formatting and redact sensitive tenant IDs before shipping.
notes: Design trade-offs: aggressive predictive models reduce cost but increase risk of underprovisioning; we prefer conservative defaults and per-tenant tuning
We will avoid opaque ML-based autoscalers in the first iteration; deterministic rules make reasoning and audit easier for enterprise customers
Consider future extension: add model-aware scaling (route different model variants to separate pools) and per-model warm caches as an explicit resource in policy
